storyText:
After spending a long time gaming or watching videos, Kavi sits down to do something else but struggles to focus. Kavi wanted to concentrate on the next activity. Kavi's attention feels scattered and their mind feels tired. While wondering what to do, Kavi noticed a round smooth stone nearby. The old thought came quickly: "My attention controls me.". So Kavi tried to study exactly how it worked. Kavi tried to push through it, and the feeling was still there, just as big as before. Along the way, Kavi noticed the round smooth stone again. Kavi tried again, a different way instead. Kavi tried to focus even harder, and the feeling had not gone anywhere at all. Kavi paused instead of forcing focus, and noticed what was actually pulling at their attention, realizing I can guide my attention back to what matters.

This time, Kavi took a step back and looked at it fresh — Kavi took one slow breath, then looked back at just the one thing in front of them, and this time it actually came into focus.

Kavi settled back into the thought and kept going — clearer, with the noise finally out of the way.
